description: Minimal RFC 5424 syslog collector and viewer based on DuckDB. Runs as a single, resource-friendly process.

summary.one_liner: Sloggo is a minimal syslog collector and web viewer that ingests RFC 5424 logs over TCP and UDP and stores them in DuckDB.
summary.what_it_does: Sloggo listens for syslog messages over TCP and UDP using the RFC 5424 protocol and stores them in DuckDB. It provides a web UI for searching, filtering, and tailing logs. Configuration is done through environment variables, and it runs as a single process. The README says it can parse RFC 3164 messages too, via the SLOGGO_LOG_FORMAT setting with its auto mode. Old logs are removed after a configurable retention period, which defaults to 30 days. The README also describes a health check endpoint and a backend test target run with make test.
use_cases: collect syslog from small network devices or servers
view and search real-time logs in a browser
lightweight log aggregation for a home lab or small team
replace a heavy ELK stack for small log volumes
how_to_run: docker run --name sloggo -p 5514:5514/udp -p 6514:6514 -p 8080:8080 -e SLOGGO_LISTENERS=tcp,udp -e SLOGGO_UDP_PORT=5514 -e SLOGGO_TCP_PORT=6514 -e SLOGGO_API_PORT=8080 -v ./data:/app/.duckdb ghcr.io/phare/sloggo:latest
echo " 1 2025-08-04T12:00:00Z myhost sloggo - - - Hello, Sloggo" | nc localhost 6514
notable: Single process with minimal resource usage and configuration through environment variables
Ingests RFC 5424 syslog over both TCP and UDP
Auto mode falls back from RFC 5424 to RFC 3164 parsing
Uses DuckDB for storage, with configurable log retention
Packaged as a container image under 10 MiB compressed
caveats: Alpha release; the README says not to use it for anything serious
No security layer by default; intended for private networks or behind a secure reverse proxy
Not a high availability solution and not meant for long-term storage or critical data
